newsitem.title: USA: CME expands boneless beef futures trading rights.
newsitem.headline: CME expands boneless beef futures trading rights.

text.p: The Chicago Mercantile Exchange Board of Directors said it will allow members from all divisions to trade the soon-to-be-listed boneless beef contract.

It will entitle CME, International Monetary Market, Index and Options Market and Growth and Emerging Markets members with full seats to trade and broker boneless beef contracts for a minimum of two years.
The Board approved a June 16 launch date for the boneless beef and boneless beef trimmings contract at its meeting Wednesday, according to a board newsletter.

IMM, IOM and GEM division members will pay lessee rates for trading and brokering the contract, and GEM members will pay lessee rate for trading and brokering its options. Participating IMM, IOM and GEM members will be entitled to continue trading for a minimum of three additional years.
Those members will also receive the differential between lessee and member clearing fees for the length of the program to use toward an equity purchase, the newsletter said.
The Board also said it waived clearing fees for the boneless contracts futures and options from launch through December 31, 1997.
